rules: Verdict rule. An option is better than another on a consequence when the paired mean difference lies beyond the threshold in the consequence's good direction, worse when it lies beyond it in the other, and unclear otherwise. The threshold is the two-sided Student t quantile, with one degree of freedom fewer than the rollouts, at the family level of 5 percent shared out over the consequences (Bonferroni), in standard errors. The weighted line weights the hypotheses' paired differences rollout by rollout, since a rollout's worlds share their seed, and takes the mean and standard error of those sums. An option dominates another when it is better on at least one consequence and worse on none, and the two trade off when it is better on one and worse on another. A line's ranking is a dominance when one option dominates every other option, a trade-off when some pair trades off, a partial order when some option dominates another and no pair trades off, and no clear ranking when no pair differs clearly on any consequence.

Stability rule. A verdict, a relation to the baseline, or a ranking is stable only if it is the same on every hypothesis line and the weighted line, under every continuation style, and at every research tick. Otherwise it is uncertain, and the report names what it depends on. The hindsight line and the reference tick enter none of this.
